proposal.explanation: Fixed three functional defects in the axis_switch module: 1) In source interfaces, the ready signal read from int_axis_tready used an incorrect stride (M_COUNT instead of S_COUNT), causing misrouting when source and destination counts differ. 2) In destination interfaces, the valid signal mux used an incorrect stride (S_COUNT instead of M_COUNT) when reading from int_axis_tvalid. 3) The ready signal write to int_axis_tready used a shift of a 1-bit value, which cannot produce a one-hot vector; replaced with a generate-for loop that assigns each bit correctly. These changes ensure correct cycle-exact behavior for all parameterized configurations.

proposal.explanation: Two functional repairs: 1) Fixed CL_S_COUNT and CL_M_COUNT parameters to avoid zero-width vectors when S_COUNT or M_COUNT is 1. 2) Corrected the m_ifaces generate block: the acknowledge signal now uses the destination-side signals (m_axis_tvalid, m_axis_tready, m_axis_tlast) to ensure the grant is released only after the last beat is accepted downstream. The request assignment remains per-source. The inner for-loop now only assigns request; acknowledge is assigned as a vector. This matches the intended cycle-exact behavior of the parameterized stream switch.

proposal.explanation: Fixed two issues: 1) CL_S_COUNT and CL_M_COUNT parameters could be zero when S_COUNT or M_COUNT is 1, causing zero-width vectors. Changed them to have a minimum width of 1. 2) The m_ifaces generate block had numerous undefined signals and incorrect connections. Rewrote it to properly declare request/acknowledge/grant signals, instantiate the arbiter, mux data from the granted source, drive ready signals, and connect the output register. The new implementation uses grant_encoded to select the granted source's signals and generates request/acknowledge based on int_axis_tvalid and the muxed last/ready.
